precepts.text: I will save the house of Joseph and bring them again, and they shall be as though I had not cast them off; I will hiss for them and gather them, and bring them again out of the land of Egypt and out of Assyria.
precepts.point: Blessed be Egypt my people and Assyria the work of my hands: the one verse they might run to for another nation, and a few chapters on the Lord beats off from the stream of Egypt and gathers one by one the children of Israel, those ready to perish in Assyria and the outcasts in Egypt, to worship at Jerusalem. My people in Egypt and Assyria means Israel in those lands, the remnant recovered the second time from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar and Hamath, Judah and Joseph brought again out of Egypt and Assyria.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
One more, just in case. “And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph, and I will bring them again to place them.” Bring them again: that is the second time, the recovering of Isaiah 11. “For I have mercy upon them: and they shall be as though I had not cast them off”: as though they had never been in captivity. “For I am the Lord their God, and will hear them.”

“And they of Ephraim shall be like a mighty man, and their heart shall rejoice as through wine: yea, their children shall see it, and be glad.” “I will hiss for them, and gather them; for I have redeemed them.” Both Judah and Joseph, Judah and Ephraim: he will gather all twelve tribes. “And they shall increase as they have increased. And I will sow them among the people: and they shall remember me in far countries; and they shall live with their children, and turn again.”

“I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt, and gather them out of Assyria.” Bring who again? All twelve tribes, out of Egypt and out of Assyria, the same as Isaiah 11:11. “And I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon; and place shall not be found for them.”

So what does “Egypt my people” and “Assyria the work of my hands” mean? It means Israel in those lands. That makes four scriptures, and there is no arguing with it. That is called precepts.

precepts.why:
Obadiah said “Benjamin shall possess Gilead”, and Zechariah shows God bringing us there: “I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt, and gather them out of Assyria; and I will bring them into the land of Gilead”. He is going to take us out of captivity and bring us into the land of Gilead. That is Obadiah 19 that was just read.

Then “and Lebanon”. Who belongs in Lebanon? Go back to Obadiah verse 20: “the captivity of this host of the children of Israel shall possess that of the Canaanites, even unto Zarephath”, and Zarephath is Lebanon. “and the captivity of Jerusalem, which is in Sepharad, shall possess the cities of the south.” Then verse 21: “And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau”, the mount of Edom.

Then “and place shall not be found for them.” There is not going to be enough room for us. Isaiah 49 says the same: “For thy waste and thy desolate places, and the land of thy destruction, shall even now be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants”. There will be too many of us. “and they that swallowed thee up shall be far away”: the nations that swallowed us up shall be far away.

Then: “The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other, shall say again in thine ears, The place is too strait for me: give place to me that I may dwell.” This place is too narrow; make room for me. That is why Christ said that in his Father's house are many mansions. Israel will come back in such numbers that the land cannot hold us.

note.label: Zechariah 10: Mine Anger Was Kindled Against the Shepherds

precepts.why:
They were troubled, because there was no shepherd. That is the condition of Israel as a nation right now, because the men our people look to for leadership are not shepherds according to the word. “His watchmen are blind: they are all ignorant, they are all dumb dogs, they cannot bark; sleeping, lying down, loving to slumber.”

A watchman is set to keep you out of harm's way, and one that cannot bark warns no one. Blind, ignorant, sleeping and loving to slumber: that is the leadership that leaves the flock going its own way, comforted in vain by idols and diviners.

note.label: Zechariah 10: Mine Anger Was Kindled Against the Shepherds

precepts.why:
“Yea, they are greedy dogs which can never have enough, and they are shepherds that cannot understand: they all look to their own way, every one for his gain, from his quarter.”

They are shepherds that cannot understand, every one looking to his own gain. They teach that the law no longer has to be kept and still ask for the tithe. That is why there is no shepherd in Israel and the flock is troubled: those who stand as shepherds are greedy dogs that can never have enough.

This explains place shall not be found for them. “For thy waste and thy desolate places, and the land of thy destruction, shall even now be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants”. “And they that swallowed thee up shall be far away”: the white man is going to be far away.

“The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other”: lost the other means the two thirds that we lost. “Shall say again in thine ears, The place is too strait for me”: it’s too narrow for us. “Give place to me that I may dwell”: make room, Lord, we need room.

“For the Lord shall comfort Zion: he will comfort all her waste places”: why? Because all Israel was wasted. “And he will make her wilderness like Eden”: he’s going to make the wilderness of Israel like Eden, “and her desert like the garden of the Lord”. So it’s going to return back to the time of Adam, the way it was.

“For the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment, and they that dwell therein shall die in like manner”: that’s destruction. “But my salvation shall be for ever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished.”

“Hearken unto me, ye that know righteousness, the people in whose heart is my law”: that’s why we got to study and keep the commandments. “Fear ye not the reproach of men”: brothers and sisters, don’t fear what the ADL has to say, the SPLC or Canary Mission; to hell with them. “Neither be ye afraid of their revilings”: don’t be afraid of their hate.

“Thy holy cities are a wilderness, Zion is a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation.” Sometimes when you read about the wilderness it’s referring to the land of Israel. Ezekiel 20 and Isaiah 11 are talking about a different wilderness, the one we’re going to walk in dryshod.

Here are the borders of the land. “In the same day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying, Unto thy seed have I given this land, from the river of Egypt”: that’s the Nile. On the map, everything on the right side of the Nile belongs to Israel. “Unto the great river, the river Euphrates”: you see the river Euphrates highlighted up there where Syria is. All that was given in promise to Abraham, for us.

What you see on the map today as Israel is not the whole land that God gave to our ancestors. “In the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give them, as the days of heaven upon the earth.” “For if ye shall diligently keep all these commandments which I command you, to do them, to love the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, and to cleave unto him; Then will the Lord drive out all these nations from before you, and ye shall possess greater nations and mightier than yourselves.”

Now here’s the point: “Every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours: from the wilderness”: on the map with the red outline, down at the bottom right after Egypt is the wilderness. “And Lebanon”: you see Lebanon up there. “From the river, the river Euphrates”: that’s up where Syria is. “Even unto the uttermost sea shall your coast be”: the uttermost sea is the Mediterranean on the far left. So God in the Bible has given us the map of our land, given to our forefathers. Lebanon is our land too; the Arabs got it now, and we’re going to take it back.

Gilead is situated in modern day Jordan: today they call it Jordan, the Bible called it Gilead. All that’s ours too, but right now the Arabs got it. The Arabs and the white man got everything, and they’re going to get blown to hell and back.

Isaiah is saying the same thing. “Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant; and Israel, whom I have chosen: Thus saith the Lord that made thee, and formed thee from the womb, which will help thee; Fear not, O Jacob, my servant; and thou, Jesurun, whom I have chosen.” The Lord is saying fear not, O Jacob; Jesurun whom I have chosen, that’s us.

“For I will pour water upon him that is thirsty, and floods upon the dry ground: I will pour my spirit upon thy seed”: that’s the Holy Spirit, poured upon thy seed, “and my blessing upon thine offspring”. Watch this: “And they shall spring up as among the grass, as willows by the water courses.” He’s comparing us waking up, this Great Awakening, to grass rising in the field.

“One shall say, I am the Lord’s; and another shall call himself by the name of Jacob”: we’re at this point now; some brothers have an alias. “And another shall subscribe with his hand unto the Lord, and surname himself by the name of Israel”: some brothers have officially changed their names altogether. So you got two levels there, but it’s all working together.

“Then shall we know, if we follow on to know the Lord”. “His going forth is prepared as the morning”: as the morning. “And he shall come unto us as the rain”: that’s that Holy Spirit raining down on us, “as the latter and former rain unto the earth”, like the end gathering seasons, the harvest and the ingathering. That’s the rain asked of the Lord in the time of the latter rain.

“Therefore hearken not ye to your prophets, nor to your diviners, nor to your dreamers, nor to your enchanters, nor to your sorcerers, which speak unto you, saying, Ye shall not serve the king of Babylon”. So even back then you had the diviners, these sorcerers, saying you didn’t have to serve the king of Babylon.

“For they prophesy a lie unto you”: see that, they prophesy a lie unto you, “to remove you far from your land; and that I should drive you out, and ye should perish.” The diviners of Zechariah 10:2 that have seen a lie are the same kind.

“What profiteth the graven image that the maker thereof hath graven it; the molten image, and a teacher of lies”: a teacher of lies comes with it. Wherever there’s an idol, you always got diviners and sorcerers that speak for these images.

The Statue of Liberty: what that image represents is democracy, all becoming one nation, one people, based upon ‘Christian’ ideals. Caesar. Mount Rushmore: people speak on their behalf on how great the forefathers of the country were, and they all had slaves. Islam, Judaism, Christianity. What comes with all of these idols are teachers of lies, men and women, black and white. Even in Islam, what comes with that dead meteorite, that stone, is a teacher of lies.

Then look at some of the diviners: why every single Christian Bible teacher is misleading you. These are some of the most famous people your mothers and fathers, sisters and brothers relish: teachers of lies, every last one of them. False teachers exposed. In 2022 they had a mass meeting, and one Negro was there, one African was there.

The shepherds that God’s anger is kindled against: “Yea, they are greedy dogs which can never have enough, and they are shepherds that cannot understand: they all look to their own way, every one for his gain”. All they care about is money.

So we can understand the goats. “And as for you, O my flock, thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I judge between cattle and cattle, between the rams and the he goats.” See that: the Lord separates Israel as rams and goats. The goats are those rebellious ones.

Why the Lord is dealing with Judah first, visiting “his flock the house of Judah”: he “chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved.” See who he chose: Judah, that’s mount Zion. That ain’t saying he don’t love the rest of y’all, but he said he chose Judah. This is why we catch all the hell, because he’s going to give us some blessings.

Out of him, which is Judah, came forth the corner: “And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”. Jesus Christ himself, out of Judah, is the chief corner stone.

Out of Judah the nail: “And I will fasten him as a nail in a sure place; and he shall be for a glorious throne to his father’s house.” Now who y’all think that’s talking about? Who’s the king? Christ, because that’s who it’s talking about.

The chapter before explains what that battle bow of Judah is. “Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope”: our brothers and sisters that were murdered, that was killed. The mothers and fathers, sisters and brothers of our people who have been murdered are hoping for a better day. Our job is to tell them to return to the stronghold: turn to the Bible and learn it the correct way. “Even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee”: God says he’s going to render double unto us.

“When I have bent Judah for me”: God said, I’m going to bend the tribe of Judah. You might see a lot of things happening to Judah; there’s a reason behind it. Judah is rebellious, and God says I’m going to bend Judah to my will, and that’s what you’re seeing right here. A large majority here is Judah. Fill “the bow with Ephraim”: and you Puerto Ricans, you Mexicans, you ain’t getting away either; he said I’m going to make you do my will. “And raised up thy sons”: I’m going to raise up the rest of the Israelites, those Mexicans, those Panamanians, to the twelve tribes of Israel.

“Against thy sons, O Greece”. What Bible are these churches not reading? Right now this is a spiritual warfare: we are against the sons of Greece, we are against Esau, Edom. God is bending us to his will. Why are you always going against the white man? Because the Bible says go against him, that’s why. “And made thee as the sword of a mighty man”: God said he’s going to make us as the sword of a mighty man.

“And the Lord shall be seen over them”: this lets you know the time period. By the time this gets physical, God said I’m going to be seen over my children, my people. So it ain’t right now, but it’s going to come. “And the Lord God shall blow the trumpet, and shall go with whirlwinds of the south”: that’s the chariots, what they call UFOs, UAPs now.

“The Lord of hosts shall defend them”: God said he’s going to defend us. “And they shall devour, and subdue with sling stones”: we’re going to devour the nations and subdue all the nations, starting with Greece. “And they shall drink, and make a noise as through wine”: we’re going to party.

“And the Lord their God shall save them in that day as the flock of his people: for they shall be as the stones of a crown”. We are his jewels, j-e-w-e-l-s; that’s what Jew comes from. “Lifted up as an ensign upon his land. For how great is his goodness, and how great is his beauty!”

The riders on horses: “I have seen servants upon horses”. That servant is that white man; he’s in the power seat, he’s on the horse. “And princes walking as servants upon the earth”: we are the princes walking as servants on the ground. We’re the nothings now, but there’s coming a day, and what we see now is just the beginning.

They shall remember me in far countries. “And it shall come to pass, when all these things are come upon thee, the blessing and the curse”: the blessing happened under King David and King Solomon; that happened already. Now we’re under the curses. “And thou shalt call them to mind among all the nations”: you Israelites shall call these things to mind among Haiti, Jamaica, Sudan, Puerto Rico, Mexico, America, Europe, “whither the Lord thy God hath driven thee”.

“And shalt return unto the Lord thy God”: that’s what we’re doing now, we’re returning to the Lord our God. “And shalt obey his voice according to all that I command thee this day, thou and thy children”: you and your children must obey, “with all thine heart, and with all thy soul”.

“That then the Lord thy God will turn thy captivity”: when we do that, when we obey, God said then I shall turn your captivity, “and have compassion upon thee, and will return and gather thee from all the nations”. Don’t worry about the Israelites scattered worldwide that you can’t even find: from there the Lord thy God will gather thee, and from there he will fetch thee. “And the Lord thy God will bring thee into the land which thy fathers possessed”. We’re going back to New Jerusalem.

I’m going to bring you into the land of Gilead, and one tribe is going to take Gilead. “And they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau; and they of the plain the Philistines: and they shall possess the fields of Ephraim, and the fields of Samaria: and Benjamin shall possess Gilead.” So what tribe is going to take Gilead? Benjamin.

Place shall not be found for them, because when we go back to the land it’s not going to be enough room for us; there’s going to be so many of us. What we see here, as great and monumental as this is, is nothing; they ain’t seen nothing yet. “For thy waste and thy desolate places, and the land of thy destruction, shall even now be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants, and they that swallowed thee up shall be far away.”

“The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other”: two-thirds of our people are going to be lost here in America. Two-thirds got to die; ain’t no damn good. “Shall say again in thine ears, The place is too strait for me”: the place is too small for us, there’s not enough room for the Israelites. “Give place to me that I may dwell”: give me more room.

“Then shalt thou say in thine heart, Who hath begotten me these”: there’s going to be so many Israelites the question is who’s begotten me all these children. We’re going to have so many children, and our people coming from far and distant lands. The party ain’t over yet.

What does it mean, he shall pass through the sea with affliction? “Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas; and to the rushing of nations, that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!” “The nations shall rush like the rushing of many waters”: so it’s comparing nations to the seas, the waters. “But God shall rebuke them, and they shall flee far off, and shall be chased as the chaff of the mountains”, “like a rolling thing before the whirlwind.” Now we got the thought: Christ passing through the sea is Christ passing through the nations.

What does it mean, walk up and down in his name? “For I will take you from among the heathen”: heathen means nations. “And gather you out of all countries”: whatever countries our people are in, I’m going to gather you, “and will bring you into your own land.” “Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you.”

“A new heart also will I give you”: that’s the spirit of God, the Holy Spirit. “And a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh. And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes”. So when it says we’re going to walk in the name of the Lord, it means we’re going to walk in his statutes, “and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them.” It’s a living God.

points: “I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt”: that’s talking about captivity. “And gather them out of Assyria”: captivity. “And I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon”: put that map back up. That’s the land of Israel: you see Lebanon at the very top and Gilead below it in the green. That’s us going into the land, and that’s different than what we read in Ezekiel 20 about the wilderness. “And place shall not be found for them.”

“Ask ye of the Lord rain in the time of the latter rain”. The latter rain comes during the harvest season, the ingathering. Asking of the Lord rain in the time of the latter rain, we’re asking for the Holy Spirit; that’s what he’s saying.
“So the Lord shall make bright clouds, and give them showers of rain, to every one grass in the field”: to every one grass in the field, meaning to every one man in the field.

There’s a whole lot in verse two. “For the idols have spoken vanity”: the idols have spoken vanity, lies. “And the diviners have seen a lie”: the diviners are the ones who speak on behalf of the idol, and they speak lies. “And have told false dreams; they comfort in vain.”

“Therefore they went their way as a flock”: therefore we, the Israelites, went our way as a flock. “They were troubled, because there was no shepherd”: our people are troubled because there’s no shepherd.

That is a major topic today: why black men don’t go to church. Because there’s no real shepherds in the church. You got feminism and homosexuality, the LGBT community, all running through there, so the real men are leaving the Christian church. Black church foolishness, LGBT, feminism: you can’t make this stuff up. This is why people don’t go to church.

“Mine anger was kindled against the shepherds”: that’s our pastors, these so-called pastors, these reverends. God is angry with them because they’re not doing what God told them to do, to gather the twelve tribes of Israel. They’re so worried about collecting money and donations and lying to the people to get it. “And I punished the goats”, because they were not doing their jobs, just like today.

The march today ruffled some feathers. Pastor Trevor Turner on Facebook had a few words to say about what he saw: ‘We the church should have gained these brothers’, ‘we have not gone after the men’, ‘the difference is they go out and get the people and we just have church inside with the doors closed’, ‘we don’t worry about them until our young men have funerals in our churches’, ‘I also take accountability for not joining a Ministry that would train me to do more’. This is a confession, a Christian confession. All these pastors say this in their head; not among themselves, but secretly, in their own mind. He’s throwing shade at all the other pastors. And that’s tonight’s class, leadership: how to do more, accountability, responsibility.

The whole point is that whole paragraph is an admission to failure. Most of our people saw us out there; they were in awe, inspired, amazed with what they saw, and he said, we’re failing, the church is failing. Only at funerals, or catering to the women, do they do something; outside of that they’re doing nothing. Oakland, California was the revolutionary place that our people believed was extinguished. He thought he extinguished revolution here; he did not. You guys marched through the streets; you are that light our people needed to see, that light that shines in the dark place. Be proud of yourselves. All praise to the Most High.

“Mine anger was kindled against the shepherds”: this is why. Poison in the black church. A popular minister: let’s sell weed in the church; you can’t make this stuff up. Woke and wicked: that’s the Christian church. A famous mega church pastor arrested for sexual assault. A pastor with a sweater and the hair giving very feminine vibes. A pastor has a thought-provoking question: black man, are you stupid? If you follow the pastors, you are.

“For the Lord of hosts hath visited his flock the house of Judah, and hath made them as his goodly horse in the battle”. He made us like a goodly horse in the battle: he made Judah into a mighty tribe.

“Out of him came forth the corner”: out of Judah came forth the corner, the chief corner stone. That’s Christ; he’s the king. “Out of him the nail”: out of Judah the nail, in a sure foundation. That’s Christ; he’s the foundation. “Out of him the battle bow”: out of Judah came the battle bow; that’s Judah coming out of there. “Out of him every oppressor together”: every oppressor is going to be destroyed.

“And they shall be as mighty men”: the Israelites shall be as mighty men. There’s going to come a transformation; the Lord is going to give us spiritual power in these days. “Which tread down their enemies in the mire of the streets in the battle”: we’re going to tread down our enemies. “And they shall fight, because the Lord is with them”: we shall fight, because the Lord is with us, and only us.

“And the riders on horses shall be confounded”: the white man is the rider of horses, those white men in the power seat, and they’re going to be confounded. They put Teddy Roosevelt on a horse and put Gad and Judah on the ground. This is just the beginning, brothers.

“And I will strengthen the house of Judah”: the Lord said, don’t worry Judah, you might be weak right now, but I’m going to strengthen you spiritually, mentally and physically. “And I will save the house of Joseph”: don’t think the Lord forgot about you; he didn’t forget about you either. “And I will bring them again to place them; for I have mercy upon them”: the Lord is having mercy upon the twelve tribes of Israel.

“And they shall be as though I had not cast them off”: it’s going to be like the Lord never sent us to America as slavery, like we never went to Haiti as slavery, like we were never conquered by the Conquistadors. It’s going to be like that never ever happened. “For I am the Lord their God, and will hear them.”

“And they of Ephraim shall be like a mighty man”: y’all see that about Ephraim? That’s you Puerto Ricans. Don’t worry, you might be fat, short and stumpy; God said you Puerto Ricans are going to be like mighty men on that day. “And their heart shall rejoice as through wine: yea, their children shall see it, and be glad”: their children are going to see Daddy, see Mommy; they’re going to see that transformation. “Their heart shall rejoice in the Lord.”

“I will hiss for them”: you know a snake hisses. Hiss has two applications: to call, and to express contempt or scorn. So God’s calling to us and expressing scorn to the other nations. I’m going to hiss for Israel. “And gather them; for I have redeemed them”: Christ ain’t redeeming all people on earth, only Judah and Joseph, Judah and Ephraim. That’s it. “And they shall increase as they have increased.”

“And I will sow them among the people: and they shall remember me in far countries”. This brother’s waking up. Some of us was that simple brother in the crowd saying, what, we’re the Israelites? You’re not dumb, you’re an Israelite. That ‘dumb Puerto Rican’? No, you’re an Israelite. That ‘dumb Mexican’? No, you’re an Israelite.
We shall remember the Lord in far countries. Believe it or not, America’s far from Jerusalem; we’re in a far country. “And they shall live with their children, and turn again.”

“I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt”: that’s America, with the chariots. “And gather them out of Assyria”: the other lands. “And I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon; and place shall not be found for them”: there ain’t going to be enough room for us.

“And he shall pass through the sea with affliction”: he is Christ, the King of Kings, Lord of Lords. The seas are the nations, so Christ is going to pass through the nations with affliction. “And shall smite the waves in the sea”: so you know what time it is. This is war; that’s what it’s saying. “And all the deeps of the river shall dry up: and the pride of Assyria shall be brought down”: the pride of this white man in the nation shall be brought down. “And the sceptre of Egypt shall depart away”: the rulership of America shall end.

“And I will strengthen them in the Lord”: the Lord said he’s going to strengthen Jacob, the twelve tribes of Israel. “And they shall walk up and down in his name, saith the Lord”: we’re going to walk up and down in his name, which means we’re going to walk in his statutes.
